set_aside.subject: R0-07 bootstrap success output
set_aside.text: the success message shows the normalized email
set_aside.question: What exact email-normalization rule determines the value printed by a successful bootstrap command?
options: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the entire address
Normalize only the domain while preserving the local part
Apply Unicode normalization in addition to case and whitespace handling
set_aside.default_guess: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the entire address using the same canonicalization used for staff-email uniqueness.

witness.initial: No staff account exists, and the deployment operator supplies ` Alice@Example.COM ` to the bootstrap command.
events: The host operator completes a successful bootstrap.
outcomes: The success message shows `Alice@example.com` or preserves the supplied casing and spacing after validation.
witness.observer: The host operator and any deployment automation consuming the message

set_aside.subject: R0-09 viewer entry
set_aside.question: What is the viewer-entry rate-limit policy: what is counted, by which key, over what window, and what observable failure is returned when the limit is reached?
options: Limit attempts per access credential
Limit attempts per source address
Limit by both credential and source address, with separate thresholds
set_aside.default_guess: Apply separate per-credential and per-source-address limits and return one concealed throttling failure with a bounded retry interval.

witness.initial: A valid viewer access link exists and has not been used or revoked.
events: One actor submits six entry attempts for that credential from six source addresses within a short interval.
The legitimate viewer then submits the valid credential.
outcomes: A per-source limit permits the legitimate viewer to enter.
A per-credential limit has exhausted the credential's allowance and refuses the legitimate viewer.

set_aside.subject: R0-09 viewer sign-out transport guard
set_aside.text: a viewer sign-out is refused unless it comes from the portal's own public origin
set_aside.question: What request evidence proves that sign-out comes from the public origin, how is that origin selected when trusted configuration contains more than one origin, and what happens when the relevant browser header is absent or malformed?
options: Require an exact canonical `Origin` match
Accept a matching `Origin`, or a matching `Referer` when `Origin` is absent
Use Fetch Metadata and host information as additional or alternative evidence
set_aside.default_guess: Require a syntactically valid `Origin` whose canonical origin exactly matches one configured portal public origin; otherwise return the same concealed refusal.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid session cookie and is using the genuine portal.
events: The viewer's browser sends a sign-out request with the cookie but without an `Origin` header and with a same-origin `Referer`.
outcomes: The portal accepts the matching `Referer` and ends the session.
The portal requires `Origin` and refuses the sign-out.

set_aside.subject: R0-24 lazy manual-budget creation
set_aside.text: creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: What lifecycle and activation state does the newly created empty manual budget version have, especially when the project has no active budget or already has an active imported snapshot?
options: Create it inactive in every case
Activate it only when the project has no active budget version
Create and activate it, replacing any previously active version
set_aside.default_guess: Create it inactive when another budget version is active, and make it active only when the project has no active budget version.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version and no active budget version.
events: An assigned staff member reads the project's progress list.
A viewer with an existing grant subsequently reads the project budget.
outcomes: The empty manual version is active, so the viewer sees a manual budget with no sections.
The empty manual version is inactive, so the viewer still sees budget data as unavailable.
witness.observer: The viewer and staff reviewing budget versions

set_aside.subject: R0-24 empty manual-budget representation
set_aside.question: Which stored facts are created for this version, and how must later reads distinguish the automatically created empty version from unavailable budget data or a deliberately entered zero budget?
options: Create only an internal empty container that is not exposed as a usable budget
Create a normal EUR manual version with identity, provenance and timestamps and expose zero totals
Create a normal version but expose planned totals and progress as unavailable until a section is entered
set_aside.default_guess: Create a normal EUR manual version with generated identity, staff provenance and creation time, but report planned totals and progress as unavailable until it contains an explicit section.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget, sections or planned amounts.
events: A staff member reads its progress list, causing the empty version to be created.
A viewer then reads the project's budget summary.
outcomes: The viewer sees a real manual budget totaling EUR 0.00.
The viewer sees budget values as unavailable because no planned amount was supplied.

set_aside.subject: R0-24 progress-list read and lazy creation
set_aside.text: a staff read of a project's progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: Are creation of the empty version, its required audit record, and production of the progress-list response one atomic action, and what does the read return if any of those steps fails?
options: Roll back the creation and fail the read if any step fails
Commit the version even if producing the progress response later fails
Return the progress list even if version creation or auditing fails
set_aside.default_guess: Treat creation and its audit as atomic prerequisites of the read; roll them back and return a storage-unavailable failure if either cannot complete.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version, and the staff member is authorized to read progress.
events: The staff member requests the progress list.
The version is inserted, but writing its audit record or completing the progress query fails.
The staff member retries the read after storage recovers.
outcomes: The first transaction rolled back, so the retry performs the one initial creation.
The empty version survived the failed read, so the retry observes an already existing version, potentially without its required audit.
witness.observer: The retrying staff member and an auditor

set_aside.subject: R0-24 concurrent lazy initialization
set_aside.text: when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: What must happen when two authorized staff reads concurrently observe that no manual budget version exists?
options: Both reads succeed and share one newly created version
One read succeeds and the other returns a conflict
Both reads may create separate manual budget versions
set_aside.default_guess: Enforce one lazily created manual version per project; both reads succeed and observe the same version.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version, and two assigned staff members can read its progress.
events: Both staff members request the progress list concurrently before either creation commits.
outcomes: Exactly one empty manual version is created and both reads succeed.
Two empty versions are created, or one read fails with a uniqueness conflict.
witness.observer: The two staff members and an administrator listing budget versions
